title: Head on shoulder, bouquet at waist
subject: couple
direction: Put his weight on the back foot, front hand in the trouser pocket with the thumb out, and have him pull her in with the far arm so the palm sits on her ribs rather than her hip. Ask her to tip only her head onto his shoulder: 'temple to his jacket, and don't drop the shoulder with it.' Hold the bouquet low at her waist so it breaks the white of the dress, then count them into the smile on three so you get the first one and not the fourth.
lighting: Large soft source high and camera-left, feathered off the cream backdrop so his black tux keeps texture in the lapel while she stays a stop brighter.
coaching: Almost everyone leans the whole torso instead of the head, which curves the spine and shortens her neck — cue 'only the head moves' and reset her shoulders level.

title: Bouquet at hip, shoulders touching
subject: couple
direction: Stand her on the light side with the bouquet in both hands at her far hip, stems angled down so the flower faces turn to camera. Bring him in tight behind her shoulder, near hand pocketed, far arm low across her back: 'just fingertips there, don't grip.' Then take the stiffness out of both of them with 'push your forehead an inch toward me' — it drops the chins and kills the double-chin line at the same time.
lighting: Soft frontal source slightly camera-right with a white bounce opposite, keeping the high-key backdrop clean while stopping the black tux from blocking up.
coaching: The bouquet creeps up to chest height and swallows her waistline — keep repeating 'flowers stay at the hip bone' between frames.

title: Back-to-back with crossed arms
subject: couple
direction: Set them spine to spine with the shoulder blades genuinely touching, then turn both faces the same direction toward you. He crosses his arms high on the chest and drops the outside shoulder back; she keeps the bouquet down at her thigh so it never fills the gap between them. Get the laugh with a line rather than a request — 'tell him what those shoes actually cost' — and shoot through the second wave, when the eyes crinkle and the shoulders come up.
lighting: Two soft sources flat from either side with the white background driven a stop over, so both profiles cut clean and neither casts onto the other.
coaching: They drift apart at the shoulders while laughing and it reads as two separate photos stitched together — reset the contact and say 'press back into each other.'

title: Hands joined, eyes on each other
subject: couple
direction: Angle both bodies about thirty degrees inward and join the inside hands low, arms long and loose. His outside hand goes in the pocket with the jacket buttoned and weight on the back leg; she loads her weight onto the far hip so the gown falls off the back of the dress instead of hanging flat. Then give them 'find each other's eyes and say nothing for five seconds' — the smile that arrives second is the one worth shooting.
lighting: One large window-style source camera-left at 45 degrees, soft enough to wrap the lace without flattening the texture out of it.
coaching: The joined arms bend and cramp in against their bodies and the gap closes up — ask for 'let the hands hang heavy' and check daylight through the arms.

title: Forehead touch against blown backlight
subject: couple
direction: Put them in full profile against the light and bring the foreheads together at the hairline, not nose to nose — noses collide and the whole thing turns awkward. Both pairs of hands meet low at hip height with the fingers loosely laced, elbows soft. Cue her 'close your eyes, then open them slowly and look at his mouth' — the shape of her smile changes on that beat and that is your frame.
lighting: Bare source behind them blowing the background three stops; expose for the skin so the rim rides the hairline and shoulders and everything else dissolves into haze.
coaching: Metering for the background drops both faces to silhouette — meter off her lit cheek and let the backdrop clip completely.

title: Full profile with train spread
subject: couple
direction: Set them in true profile to camera, a long step apart, with the joined hands as the only point of contact. Send her back half a pace and rotate her hips so the train sweeps out behind her into the frame — kick it into shape with your foot before you shoot, never leave it where it lands. Give both of them 'stand tall, lift the crown of your head' so the negative space between the bodies stays a clean shape, then let them smile at each other.
lighting: Soft source camera-left, three-quarter high and wide, keeping the beige seamless even so the two profiles read as one graphic silhouette.
coaching: The train collapses into a lump and his front shoe ends up standing on it — check the floor every few frames before you check the faces.

title: Walk toward camera, bouquet out
subject: couple
direction: Back them up six paces and walk them in on your count with the inside hands joined and swinging naturally. His free hand goes in the pocket; she carries the bouquet out and away from her body at almost arm's length so the skirt stays visible and the flowers get their own light. Say 'walk straight at me, don't pose, and take it at half the speed you want to' — then fire in bursts through the middle three steps.
lighting: Broad frontal soft light with low fill, so the moving tulle keeps detail and no shadow chases them across the white floor.
coaching: They accelerate and the arms go rigid — reset the pace and give the bouquet arm a physical target: 'reach the flowers out to that wall.'

title: Walking laugh, eyes off camera
subject: couple
direction: Run the same walk-in but take their eyes off you: 'look at each other the whole way and ignore me completely.' Have her carry the bouquet across the front of her body at hip height so the white flowers sit against the gown, and ask for a long stride so the skirt actually throws. Feed them one line to laugh at as they hit the mark, and shoot the beat just after the peak, when the mouths soften but the eyes are still lit.
lighting: Big frontal source slightly above eye level with a low reflector, keeping the background clean white and the shadow under the jaw open while they move.
coaching: Looking at each other makes couples stop walking — insist 'the feet keep moving even while you look' or you get a static frame with a floppy skirt.

title: Heads down, walking laugh
subject: couple
direction: Start the walk, then drop the instruction mid-stride: 'both of you look down at your feet and keep going.' The downward gaze does the work for you — it removes the camera from their heads and the laugh arrives without being asked for. Keep the inside hands joined low and his outside hand pocketed, and drop your own camera to chest height so you still get the underside of both faces instead of the tops of their heads.
lighting: Even soft frontal source with the background lit to near white, so faces angled down still catch fill and the eye sockets don't go dead.
coaching: The chins tuck too far and you lose both faces — cue 'eyes down, chin stays up' and shoot from lower rather than asking them to lift.

title: Temple kiss with bouquet low
subject: couple
direction: Bring him in behind her shoulder and turn her body slightly away from him so you keep the line of the gown, then put his near hand flat on her far waist to close the gap between the torsos. He kisses the hairline above her ear and stays there — 'hold the kiss, don't peck it.' She drops the chin, closes her eyes, and lets the bouquet hang from a straight arm at her hip: 'let the flowers get heavy.'
lighting: Soft source camera-left just above his head height so the kiss doesn't shade her eye socket, with white fill camera-right to lift the lace on the gown.
coaching: He breaks the kiss the instant he hears the shutter — tell him up front that the kiss ends when you say so, not when the camera fires.

title: Cheekbone kiss, face to camera
subject: couple
direction: This frame lives or dies on her face angle: turn her shoulders away from him but rotate her chin back toward you so the lens gets the full cheek and both sets of lashes. He kisses the cheekbone rather than the temple, mouth soft and low enough that his brow never crosses her eye. Give her 'small smile, like you're keeping a secret,' and swing the bouquet down and out to the far side so it clears her hands and reads against the dark jacket.
lighting: Large soft key camera-right, feathered so the highlight lands on her cheekbone and his navy jacket falls a stop under and separates from the wall.
coaching: His head blocks her far eye nine times out of ten — move him back an inch and lower his kiss, and never fix it by turning her.

title: Forehead resting on her hair
subject: couple
direction: No kiss in this one — he rests his brow against her temple and simply stops there. Put her front shoulder toward camera with his chest behind it and his far hand on her waist so both bodies commit to the contact instead of hovering. Tell them 'close your eyes and just breathe,' then wait ten full seconds before the first frame: the first three are performed and everything after that is real. Keep the bouquet low and out of the chest line so nothing crowds the two heads.
lighting: Soft key camera-left at head height with a large white bounce opposite, holding both faces in the same plane so neither one shadows the other.
coaching: He presses too hard and pushes her head sideways off vertical — cue 'rest, don't lean' and check her neck line before you shoot.

title: Temple kiss from behind, bouquet low
subject: couple
direction: Stand him behind her shoulder at about forty-five degrees and have him wrap both arms low across her ribs so his hands land flat, fingers together, never splayed. Tell her: 'close your eyes and turn your cheek toward him, chin stays up'. Have him press his lips to her temple and hold while she lets the bouquet drop to hip height in her far hand — shoot the second her shoulders come down.
lighting: Big soft source camera-right at head height, so her face keeps the highlight and his navy jacket goes into shadow against the white wall for separation.
coaching: His hand across her waist is the giveaway — if the fingers spread or the knuckles bunch, reset with 'flat hand, thumb hidden' before you shoot.

title: Tuxedo lean with hand in pocket
subject: couple
direction: Put her front-and-centre with her weight on the back foot and the train swept behind her toward camera-left, then step him in half a pace behind her shoulder. Tell him: 'left hand in the pocket, thumb out, and lean your head onto hers — not your whole body'. Bring her bouquet up to belly-button height so it breaks the white of the dress, then get both chins toward the lens on a count of three.
lighting: Broad soft key from camera-left with a white bounce opposite, keeping the black tux from blocking up while the seamless stays a stop brighter.
coaching: Full-length shots die from bad feet — check she isn't standing flat with both toes at the lens, and fan the train with your own foot before you commit.

title: Arms-around-waist laugh, both to camera
subject: couple
direction: Line him up directly behind her and have him bring both arms around her waist so his hands meet just under the bouquet — no daylight between their bodies. Say: 'squeeze her once, then whisper the worst thing you can think of'. Shoot the laugh on the rebound rather than the punchline, and keep her front foot crossed slightly over the back so the fitted skirt reads as one clean line.
lighting: Soft frontal key just off-axis camera-left with a large fill card right, so neither of the two big smiles picks up an unflattering nose shadow.
coaching: Wide open smiles go stiff by the third frame — if the eyes stop crinkling, break the pose completely and rebuild it rather than asking for 'one more'.

title: Temple-to-temple with hand in pocket
subject: couple
direction: Stand them shoulder to shoulder with his far hand in his trouser pocket and his near arm behind her back, hand resting on her waist where the camera can just see it. Tell them: 'lean your heads in until they touch, then both look at me — not at each other'. Hold the bouquet low against her hip in her outside hand so it doesn't crowd the space between their bodies.
lighting: Soft key slightly above eye level from camera-left, feathered off the white background so the charcoal check keeps its texture instead of going flat.
coaching: Height gaps ruin the head lean — if she has to tilt hard to reach him, stand her on a half-step or ask him to widen his stance and drop two inches.

title: Stacked profiles, her eyes to camera
subject: couple
direction: Put his shoulder into the frame edge and turn him to full profile facing across the lens, then bring her cheek in behind his so the two heads stack rather than sit side by side. Tell her: 'his ear is your anchor — stay right there and give me your eyes, not your chin'. Focus on her near eye and let him fall soft in the foreground; a half-inch of separation between their faces is the whole shot.
lighting: Window-soft source behind and camera-right, wrapping onto her face and blowing the background to near-white so the veil disappears into it.
coaching: At this distance the wrong focus plane kills it — pull back a hair and confirm you have her lashes sharp, not his beard.

title: Cheek kiss over the shoulder
subject: couple
direction: Angle her body forty-five degrees off camera and bring him in behind her far shoulder so his face crosses just above it. Cue him: 'kiss her cheekbone and stay there, eyes closed'. Then cue her: 'you stay on me — big smile, chin down an inch' — the whole picture is that she reacts to him while giving you the eyes, so give the two instructions separately, not at once.
lighting: Soft key camera-right about a foot above her eyeline, letting his navy jacket go a stop darker on the left so the two faces stay the brightest thing in frame.
coaching: He will drift too high and end up kissing her ear — put your finger on your own cheekbone and say 'here' before the first frame.

title: Hand on lapel, heads tipped together
subject: couple
direction: Turn him square to the lens and bring her in against his side, then give her hands a job: near hand up over his far shoulder, other hand closed around his forearm at his chest. Say: 'tip your head onto his shoulder until it lands, then relax the hand — hold him, don't grip him'. Ask them both for a closed-lip smile and let his chin stay level while hers drops toward him.
lighting: High soft key straight on with a touch of camera-left bias, keeping the pale linen suit and the lace gown from merging into the white background.
coaching: A clenched fist on the lapel reads as tension every time — call it out and ask for 'soft fingers, thumb over the top'.

title: Arms crossed, shoulder-to-shoulder laugh
subject: couple
direction: Stand them side by side with a couple of inches between them, him with arms crossed and weight on one hip, her leaning her near shoulder into his so only the shoulders touch. Tell them: 'lean into each other until you feel contact, then both laugh at me'. Keep her bouquet high against her ribs in both hands and ask him for one knee soft so the crossed arms don't stiffen his whole frame.
lighting: Even, flat frontal light with a broad source close to the lens axis — a full-length pose on white needs the floor lit too or their shoes disappear.
coaching: Crossed arms plus a big laugh usually pulls his shoulders up to his ears; reset with 'drop the shoulders, keep the arms' and shoot immediately.

title: Bouquet held low, body angled off-lens
subject: bride
direction: Turn her body about thirty degrees away from the lens, then bring her face back to you so the near shoulder leads and the far one falls behind it. Hand her the bouquet at both hands, held low at the hip and tilted slightly toward camera so you see flowers, not stems. Cue her: 'elbows away from your ribs, one inch' — that gap is what keeps the arms from flattening against the bodice.
lighting: Large soft source camera-left at forty-five degrees, close enough to wrap the collarbones and give the lace bodice raking detail.
coaching: Bouquets get lifted to the chest under nerves, which hides the waist and the dress — keep resetting the height at the hip bone every few frames.

title: Ballgown standing, train fanned behind
subject: bride
direction: Set the skirt first — walk her into position, then fan the train out behind and to her left so it makes a wide teardrop under the lights. Put her weight on the back foot, body angled slightly camera-left, and say: 'stand tall, shoulders back and down, then breathe out'. Bring the bouquet to her far hip in both hands so it sits against the bodice seam rather than floating in the middle of the skirt.
lighting: Soft key from camera-left with a gentle background gradient behind her, so the ivory silk skirt separates from the wall instead of merging with it.
coaching: Shoot from too low and a ballgown swallows her — keep the camera at chest height or above and never tilt up.

title: Veil lifted overhead into the sweep
subject: bride
direction: Have her raise both arms overhead and catch the veil just above her hairline, elbows soft and slightly forward so you keep a triangle of light between arm and body. Tell her: 'eyes closed, chin up and smile like you got away with something'. Have an assistant throw the veil from camera-right on a count of three and fire a burst as it passes overhead — you want it arcing out to one side, not draped over her face.
lighting: Soft key from the front with the throw side backlit, so the tulle lights up as translucent rather than reading as a grey smear.
coaching: Raised arms go straight and stiff within seconds and the underarms take over the frame — keep the elbows bent and shoot the first two throws only.

title: Veil held wide, gaze down
subject: bride
direction: Give her the veil edge in each hand and ask her to open her arms out and slightly forward until the tulle makes a wide curtain either side of the gown. Cue her: 'look down at your feet and smile at them, not at me'. Keep her hips angled a touch camera-left with the weight on the back leg so the satin skirt keeps one long unbroken line to the puddled train.
lighting: Soft frontal source high and slightly left, with the background lifted a half stop so the sheer veil holds shape against the white instead of vanishing.
coaching: Arms held out too wide pull her shoulders forward and round her back — cap the spread at shoulder width and ask for 'chest open, chin down'.

title: Veil lifted overhead in both hands
subject: bride
direction: Put the veil edges in both hands and have her raise them just above head height with soft elbows, so the tulle arches over her instead of collapsing onto her hair. Cue her: 'lift it, then look at me like you just caught it.' Keep the chin level and the shoulders pressed down, and shoot the beat immediately after the tulle stops rising, while the smile is still involuntary.
lighting: Large soft source straight on and slightly high, so the tulle lights from the front and glows rather than throwing hard shadow lines across her face.
coaching: Her hands creep too far apart and the veil goes flat across the frame — say 'hands closer together, right above your ears' to rebuild the arch.

title: Mermaid gown with bouquet at hip
subject: bride
direction: Turn her hips forty-five degrees off the lens and load every bit of weight onto the back foot — 'front toe just touching the floor' — so the mermaid seam sits across the hip instead of running straight down. Have her carry the bouquet on the far hip with a loose wrist, stems angled down, and let the near hand rest flat along the thigh with the fingers together. Then reset the shoulders and ask for a level look straight down the barrel: 'chin to me, no smile, just breathe out.'
lighting: Single large octabox at camera-left, feathered past her so the lace rakes across the bodice and the cyc drops half a stop behind the train.
coaching: Fitted gowns punish a squared-up stance — if the silhouette reads flat, rotate her another fifteen degrees and re-check that back foot before you shoot again.

title: Sheath gown, bouquet at waist
subject: bride
direction: Have her hold the bouquet in one hand at natural waist, stems dropping down and slightly across the body, and push the other arm straight down but off the ribs — 'make a gap you could see light through under your arm.' Send the near hip toward the lens and bring the chin down a fraction toward that same shoulder. Kill the posed mouth last: 'let your lips come apart, don't smile.'
lighting: Broad softbox close in on camera-right with a white v-flat opposite, keeping the shadow side of the gown clean so no seam goes grey.
coaching: The free arm glues itself back to the waist and adds an inch to her — reset it every frame, it drifts within two shots.

title: Low bouquet over fanned train
subject: bride
direction: Set the train first — fan it wide behind her, then have her step forward two inches so it stays spread instead of creeping back under the hem. Both hands go onto the bouquet at hip height with the stems hanging free and the elbows just off the body, so you keep a triangle of light either side of her waist. Cue the face last: 'small smile, like you're about to say something' — that stops the held grin.
lighting: Two large sources at forty-five degrees either side, one a stop hotter camera-right, so the satin keeps a gradient instead of blowing out to flat white.
coaching: Hands stacked too high hide the waist and the bodice seam — drop the bouquet until her wrists sit level with the hip bone.

title: Open back over-shoulder glance
subject: bride
direction: Walk her away from you until her back is square to the lens and the open back is the whole subject, then turn only the head — 'shoulders stay exactly where they are, just bring your chin to your shoulder.' Ask her to drop the far shoulder so the spine reads as one clean line and the strap doesn't bunch. Shoot the moment she finds your eyes, not the moment she arrives.
lighting: Push the background two stops over with a light behind her, then a soft fill just off-axis so the lace across the back keeps its texture instead of dissolving.
coaching: Most brides rotate the whole torso and you lose the back entirely — hold a hand up as a marker and say 'keep your hips pointed at the wall'.

title: Skirt gathered, glance over shoulder
subject: bride
direction: Point her forty-five degrees away from you and have her gather a handful of skirt at the back of the hip and lift it an inch — that lift is what separates the tulle layers. Then the head comes back over the near shoulder while the body stays put: 'eyes to me last, everything else stays.' Keep talking while you shoot so the smile arrives as a reaction rather than something she holds.
lighting: One big source high at camera-left with a low bounce on the right to open the underside of the tulle, which otherwise goes muddy grey.
coaching: The gathering hand turns into a claw inside two seconds — 'long fingers, like you're holding a glass of water' fixes it in one try.

title: Low bouquet with skirt pinched
subject: bride
direction: Have her carry the bouquet low and slightly across the body at the far hip, arm straight but loose, then pinch a fold of skirt with the other hand and pull it just off the leg so the silk breaks. Weight goes forward onto the near foot so the fabric drapes down one side rather than hanging dead centre. Take the smile away for this one: 'jaw loose, look right into the lens, don't perform' — it lives on stillness.
lighting: Single scrimmed source dead front and slightly above, deliberately flat so the silk stays soft and no crease reads as a shadow.
coaching: Both hands drift to the same height and the frame goes symmetrical and dull — keep the bouquet a hand-span lower than the skirt hand.

title: Skirt swept out one arm
subject: bride
direction: Bouquet into the hand nearest you at hip height, then send the far arm out and slightly back with the fingers holding the hem so the skirt opens into a sweep. Get her weight forward: 'push into your front leg like you're about to walk.' Chin stays level and the gaze goes straight down the lens — the arm carries the drama, the face does nothing.
lighting: Large source high at camera-right, feathered down the skirt so the swept fabric gets a gradient and the cyc behind stays clean light grey.
coaching: A locked straight arm makes it read as a curtsy — call 'soft elbow, and pull the fabric back, not out to the side'.

title: Veil thrown past dropped chin
subject: bride
direction: Have an assistant throw the cathedral veil past her from behind on your count, and tell her to lift the near arm loosely into the tulle as it passes — that arm is what stops the veil reading as a flat sheet. The bouquet hangs low in the other hand, stems down, no grip against the ribs. Give her the head first: 'eyes down toward your far shoulder, chin follows, and hold it' — then fire through the whole throw.
lighting: Bare head behind and to the side to backlight the tulle, with a big scrim on her front so the veil glows without her face falling into shadow.
coaching: Everyone shoots the peak and gets a limp veil — start firing before the throw lands and keep the frame where the fabric is still rising.

title: Veil spread wide arms out
subject: bride
direction: Put a veil edge in each hand and send both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms rolled slightly down so the tulle hangs as a wing instead of bunching at the wrist. The bouquet stays pinned at the waist by the forearms: 'squeeze it in with your elbows, your hands only hold the veil.' Ask for a flat level look and a small chin lift — 'own it, chin up one centimetre, don't smile.'
lighting: Broad frontal source for her face plus a low kicker on each side so both veil panels separate from the grey background instead of dissolving into it.
coaching: Her arms sag within two seconds and the wings collapse — count her in, take three frames, let her drop the arms, then repeat.

title: Bouquet at hip, chin turned away
subject: bride
direction: Angle her body across the frame and bring both hands onto the bouquet at hip height with the stems hanging free below her fingers. Then take the eyes off you completely: 'turn your chin toward the window and stop where I can still see both your eyes.' Leave the veil alone — nobody touches it, it just trails down the far side and gives you the vertical.
lighting: One large soft source at camera-right so the turned face is lit short, and the shadow side gives the lace bodice some depth against the wall.
coaching: Over-turning the chin loses the far eye and flattens the nose against the cheek — stop the turn early and check the catchlight before you commit.

title: Ballgown quarter-turn with low bouquet
subject: bride
direction: Quarter-turn her toward the light with the back foot planted and the front knee pressed softly into the skirt, so the ballgown gets a front edge instead of reading as a bell. The bouquet drops low in the outside hand and rests against the skirt; the other hand goes behind the hip so the arm never cuts across the waist. Give her a point to look at just past your shoulder and cue: 'small breath in, then let the smile come halfway.'
lighting: Soft source high at camera-left with a low reflector on the right lifting the skirt, otherwise the tulle greys out under its own volume.
coaching: A ballgown swallows the waist — before you shoot, check the bouquet arm is clear of the body and the bodice seam is still visible.

title: Seated on floor with fanned train
subject: bride
direction: Have her sit on the floor with both legs folded to her far side, hip on the ground, then reach in and sweep the train out in a wide arc behind her before you shoot. Tell her to push the floor away with her supporting hand so she sits tall: 'lift out of your waist, don't lean back.' Bring the bouquet up to rest against her forearm at rib height and cue 'tip your head toward your near shoulder, eyes stay on me.'
lighting: Large soft source high and camera-left, feathered down so the light falls off across the skirt and the white gown keeps texture instead of blowing out.
coaching: Sitting on the hip makes most brides slump and shorten the neck; reset her by asking for one deep breath in with the shoulders rolled back before every frame.

title: High-angle seated with circled skirt
subject: bride
direction: Stand on a step ladder and shoot down while she kneels back onto her heels, then have an assistant pull the tulle out into a full circle around her so the skirt reads as a ring. Ask her to drop her far hand flat onto the fabric and lay the bouquet in front of her knees: 'let your fingers rest, don't grip.' Then cue 'turn your shoulders away from me, chin follows last, eyes come back up to the lens' so the body twists but the face stays open.
lighting: Broad overhead source just behind camera, slightly camera-right, so the skirt reads bright and even and the shadow under her chin stays shallow at this angle.
coaching: From above the chin lifts and you get nostril; ask her to bring her forehead toward you a couple of centimetres and lengthen the back of the neck.

title: Wall lean with crossed ankles
subject: groom
direction: Put his far shoulder blade against the wall, both hands into the trouser pockets with thumbs out, then cross the near ankle over the far one so the legs make a clean line. Tell him 'push your weight into the back foot, the front foot is just resting' or he will look propped and stiff. Angle his chest thirty degrees off the wall and cue 'look past my shoulder at the door and think of something that actually makes you laugh.'
lighting: Soft key from camera-left at 45 degrees with a low fill, so the tuxedo lapel catches an edge and the black separates from the warm wall.
coaching: Hands buried to the wrist bunch the jacket and widen the hips; leave the thumbs and first knuckles visible outside the pocket.

title: Wall lean looking off-frame
subject: groom
direction: Same lean as the classic wall shot but open the jacket and lose the tie, then turn his head all the way into profile away from camera. Say 'chin toward your far shoulder until you can't see me at all, then come back one centimetre' so you keep the jawline without cutting off the eye. Ask for the shoulders to stay square to camera while the head turns: 'shoulders stay, head goes.'
lighting: Flat soft frontal source with a white wall bounce, keeping the shadow side open so the black suit still shows the shoulder seam against white.
coaching: A full profile with an open collar exposes the neck and reads slumped; ask him to press the back of his head lightly toward the wall to lengthen it.

title: Square stance with clasped hands
subject: groom
direction: Stand him square to camera on a clean white sweep, feet a shoulder-width apart with one foot half a step forward, and clasp both hands loosely at belt height. Cue 'hold your own wrist, not your fingers' so the hands stay long instead of turning into a fist. Then tell him 'weight onto the back leg, roll your shoulders back once, and smile at me on three' and shoot immediately after the roll.
lighting: Two large sources at 45 degrees either side, balanced within a stop, so the tuxedo holds edge detail on both sides against the white background.
coaching: A symmetrical stance goes wooden fast; break it by asking for a slight turn of one hip toward camera so the trouser line stays alive.

title: Hip lift with bouquet raised
subject: couple
direction: Have him take her onto his near hip with both forearms under her thigh, and tell him 'lift from your legs and lock your elbows in against your ribs, don't hold her out.' She keeps her inside arm hooked behind his shoulder for security and throws the bouquet arm straight up: 'reach for the ceiling and let your hand open at the top.' Count them in loudly and shoot in a burst — the good frame is the second or third, when the laugh is real and her back foot has kicked up.
lighting: Single large soft source camera-left, high enough to keep her raised arm and the bouquet lit rather than falling into the background.
coaching: Most couples wobble on the way up and you shoot the strain, not the joy; reset, tell him to plant both feet before lifting, and only run this for three takes.

title: Hand behind his neck, foreheads close
subject: couple
direction: Bring him in behind her near shoulder, his hand in his pocket so his body stays quiet, and have her reach her near arm up and back to cup the nape of his neck. Cue her 'pull him in gently until your temples touch' and give him one line to sell the laugh: 'tell her the thing you were nervous about this morning.' Keep the bouquet low at her hip so it frames the bottom of the crop instead of blocking her body.
lighting: Soft frontal key camera-right with white bounce opposite, clean and even so the high-key background stays pure behind both faces.
coaching: Her raised elbow will swing forward and cover his chin; ask her to drive that elbow back and down so it opens the gap between the faces.

title: Embrace from behind, bride to camera
subject: couple
direction: Stand him a half step behind and to her left, wrapping both arms low around her waist with his hands stacked in front of her hip bone. Tell him 'press your cheek into her hair and close your eyes' — his face is the quiet half of the frame. She holds the bouquet against her far hip, drops her near shoulder toward camera and looks straight down the lens: 'weight onto the back foot, chin down a fraction, nothing in the eyes but calm.'
lighting: Large soft key camera-right feathered across the gown so the mermaid skirt keeps its fold detail and his black tuxedo goes half a stop darker for separation.
coaching: His hands clamped high across her stomach flatten her waist; slide them down onto the hip bone and angle the fingers so they read as a line, not a block.

title: Full lift with veil flowing
subject: couple
direction: Shoot this one in true profile so the veil has somewhere to travel. He lifts her clear of the floor with both arms under her hips and pulls her chest to his; she hooks both arms over his shoulders with the bouquet hanging behind his back. Cue them 'foreheads together, noses almost touching, eyes on each other, and do not look at me' — then have an assistant throw the veil from behind and shoot as it falls, telling her 'point your toes and let the back knee bend.'
lighting: Bright high-key from behind and above, effectively backlighting the veil so the tulle glows and reads translucent against the white.
coaching: The lift usually collapses before the veil settles; call the throw and the lift on the same count and be ready to shoot within two seconds.

title: Standing kiss with trailing veil
subject: couple
direction: Set her weight fully on the back foot and let her lean away a few degrees; he steps his far leg back and bends toward her so his shoulders angle down into the kiss. Give him the line 'come in from slightly above her, tilt your head to your right so I still see both faces.' Have her hold the bouquet out and away from her body at waist height and say 'kiss and hold it — stay there for four counts, don't peck.' Lay the veil and train out along the floor toward camera before you shoot.
lighting: Soft directional key camera-left, slightly high, so the veil layers stay separated and the white jacket does not merge with the background.
coaching: Kissing poses collapse into pressed lips and tension in the jaw; tell them to smile into it and stop just short of contact, which reads warmer than a real kiss.

title: Cheek kiss with hand on shoulder
subject: couple
direction: He comes in from behind her far shoulder with one hand in his pocket and the other arm across her waist, and kisses her cheekbone — not her ear, not her mouth. Cue her 'let your eyes close, chin down toward the flowers, and just enjoy it' so the smile arrives on its own instead of being posed. Ask her to lift her near hand onto his shoulder with the fingers relaxed, and keep the bouquet held out and low so it does not hide the bodice.
lighting: Soft window-style key from camera-left with a large white fill right, letting the veil trail into open shadow so it separates from the white wall.
coaching: He tends to kiss too low and hide his own face behind her head; move the kiss up to the top of the cheekbone so both of his eyes stay visible.

title: Bride seated, groom standing behind
subject: couple
direction: Sit her on the front third of the chair, knees angled away from camera, and spread the skirt forward so it fills the base of the frame. He stands behind the far side of the chair with his near hand resting on the chair back and the other in his pocket — tell him 'lean your hip into the chair, don't stand at attention.' Bring the bouquet onto her lap and cue both of them together: 'shoulders toward each other, chins back to me, and breathe out before I shoot.'
lighting: Broad soft key camera-left with fill from the right, high enough to keep the seated face lit at the same level as his standing one.
coaching: The height gap makes this read like a school photo if they stand and sit in the same plane; stagger him half a step behind and turn his torso in toward her.

title: Underarm spin with skirt sweep
subject: couple
direction: Put his hand up high, palm down, and give her two fingers to hold — she turns away from him under the arch, never toward him. Tell her to pinch the outer layer of the skirt with her free hand and throw it low and wide as she steps: 'sweep it out, then keep walking'. Hand him the bouquet in his outside hand so it hangs at knee height and stops fighting the dress. Shoot the back half of the turn, when her front foot lands and the fabric is still travelling.
lighting: One large octabox high and camera-left, feathered across the floor so the flying skirt keeps texture instead of blowing to paper white.
coaching: The classic miss is firing at the top of the turn while the dress is still collapsed — count her through two full spins and only shoot the second.

title: Overhead joined hands mid-laugh
subject: couple
direction: Join their hands overhead but have her straighten that arm all the way and keep her shoulders square to you — near-frontal reads as celebration, ballroom-profile reads as a dance lesson. Ask her to grab a fistful of skirt low at her hip and let it drag rather than fly, so the movement lives in the arm, not the hem. He steps across behind her with the bouquet hanging in his far hand and his chin dropped toward her. Then feed her something she'll actually laugh at — 'tell him what the shoes cost' — and shoot through the laugh.
lighting: Broad frontal soft source from a 7-foot umbrella just above camera, so no shadow pins their joined hands to the white seamless.
coaching: Eyes-closed laughs are lovely but you still need one frame with an eye in it — call 'look up at your hand' the second the laugh peaks.

title: Back-to-back floor sit, knees up
subject: couple
direction: Sit them spine to spine on the floor, both knees up, each hugging their own shins so the arms make matching triangles. Tell them to press through the shoulder blades — 'lean into each other, don't hold yourself up' — or a gap opens and they read as two separate portraits. Now split the heads: each turns back over the near shoulder toward the lens and holds a closed-mouth smile, chins level. Lay the bouquet on the floor in front of her knee so the bottom of the frame isn't dead space.
lighting: Large soft source high and frontal with the white floor bouncing back up, which is what keeps the underside of two upturned faces open.
coaching: Watch the lower backs — if you can see seamless between them, have both shuffle their hips back two inches and reset.

title: Floor sit with bouquet in lap
subject: couple
direction: Get her down first: legs folded to her far side, hip on the floor, then fan the gown out toward the camera-left edge before anyone else moves. He sits in behind her shoulder with his outside knee up and drapes that forearm over the knee — 'let the hand go dead, don't grip your knee'. Bring the heads together until the temples almost touch and give you both sets of eyes. She holds the bouquet at her lap and tips it toward the lens so you see faces of flowers, not stems.
lighting: Single large source straight over camera and slightly high; the white floor does the fill and stops the gown's underside going grey.
coaching: His raised knee crowds her shoulder if he sits too close — leave a hand's width so his jacket isn't pressed into her arm.

title: Bride leaning back into groom, seated
subject: couple
direction: Same floor setup, but here she gives him her weight — open his front shoulder and tell him 'let her land on you'. Her hands fold loose and empty in her lap, legs tucked to camera-left, so the skirt sweeps as one continuous shape across the bottom third of the frame. He tucks his chin beside her ear and rests his forearm over the raised knee; both look straight down the lens. Put the bouquet on the floor at her far side instead of in her hands — free hands make it read as resting, not presenting.
lighting: Broad soft key slightly camera-right so his dark jacket keeps a defined edge against the white rather than flattening into it.
coaching: Lean too far back and her chin lifts and the jawline goes — cue 'weight back, chin forward an inch' and it comes right.

title: Cradle carry with bouquet
subject: couple
direction: Have him scoop under her knees and carry the weight on his hips, not his arms — 'stand up tall first, then pick her up'. She hooks her near arm around the back of his neck and clamps the bouquet against her far hip, which fills the outside of the frame where you'd otherwise have empty seamless. Ask her to drop her head back onto his shoulder and laugh out loud on three; the heels kick up by themselves. Pre-set your exposure — you get about fifteen good seconds before his arms start to shake.
lighting: Large source camera-left at 45 degrees, raised high enough to clear the lift so both faces stay lit at their new height.
coaching: The lift dies the moment he leans back to counterbalance — keep his spine stacked and knees soft, and shoot from slightly low so he doesn't look folded.

title: Train reveal with glance back
subject: couple
direction: Turn her fully away from the lens so the back of the gown and the whole train face you, and walk the train out with your foot before she settles into anything. He comes in from her far side, closes both arms around her waist and holds the bouquet in his outside hand at her hip. Give her the head move on its own: 'chin over your shoulder, eyes to me, stop when I say' — take her to three-quarters, not full profile. He keeps his eyes closed with his nose in her temple so there's only one gaze in the frame.
lighting: Soft key camera-left and slightly behind her, raking across the lace so the beading and the length of the train hold detail.
coaching: The train bunches at her heels after every small shift — reset it every third frame, it moves far more than couples realise.

title: Open-back gown, hand to lapel
subject: couple
direction: Same back-of-gown geometry as the last one, but nobody looks at you — keep the whole exchange inside the frame. She brings her near hand up to his collar with the fingers relaxed on the lapel and turns her face up toward his, which gives you the jaw and neck line against the open back. His hand goes flat on her waist with the thumb hidden and he comes in nose to cheekbone, eyes down. Tell her: 'hold the bouquet down and away from your hip' so the flowers sit clean against the seamless instead of merging with the dress.
lighting: Key camera-right, feathered off her bare back so the skin doesn't run half a stop hotter than the ivory lace.
coaching: A clawed hand on the lapel is the giveaway that she's gripping — ask her to touch with the pads only and let the wrist soften.

title: Bouquet up, fist up, leaning in
subject: couple
direction: Send the energy out to the edges: her bouquet arm goes straight overhead on her outside, his fist punches up on his outside, and both inside arms stay wrapped around the other's waist. He leans in behind her shoulder and lets his weight drop onto his back foot so his head tips toward hers — 'lean on her, you're leaving together'. Count them in and take the noise: 'big loud YES on three'. Frame wide enough that neither raised hand clips the top edge, and give the ballgown room at the bottom.
lighting: Even broad frontal soft light, source high enough that the raised arms don't throw shadow back across their faces.
coaching: They raise the arms and then freeze — keep talking and shoot the second and third go, the first attempt is always stiff.

title: Veil sweep with lifted heel
subject: couple
direction: Two counts: he takes her waist with both hands and plants first, then she throws the veil up and across with her outside arm in one arc. Tell her 'throw it over your head, don't wave it' — one committed sweep opens the tulle, a wobble just makes it a rag. As the veil goes up she pops the far heel off the floor and arches back into his hands, chin up toward him, both laughing at each other. Fire a burst; you are keeping the single frame where the veil is fully open and her heel is still airborne.
lighting: Big soft key camera-left plus a bare head behind them punching through the tulle, or the veil renders grey instead of glowing.
coaching: If he isn't genuinely taking her weight she'll stiffen the standing leg to stay up and the arch dies — have him step in close and lock his elbows before she moves.

title: Cheek kiss, hand in pocket
subject: couple
direction: Build his stance first — one hand in the trouser pocket with the thumb out, weight on the back foot, front knee soft, far arm around her waist. She steps up behind his shoulder, drapes her near arm across the back of his shoulders and kisses him on the cheekbone, not the jaw. Then split the attention: 'don't turn to her, react to me' — he grins down the lens while she stays on his cheek. Keep her bouquet low in her outside hand so it never crosses the waist of the gown.
lighting: Soft key camera-left at 45 with a white v-flat opposite; an ivory suit against an ivory gown needs that fill or his lapels go grey.
coaching: Hand-in-pocket fails when the whole hand vanishes and the elbow flares — thumb stays out, elbow stays near the ribs.

title: Symmetric arms-up cheer
subject: couple
direction: Square them both to the lens, shoulders touching, feet under the hips — this frame is symmetrical on purpose, so no staggered stance. Her outside arm goes up with the bouquet, his outside arm goes up in a fist, and both inside arms wrap the other's waist so the centre of the frame stays closed. Cue the sound rather than the expression: 'shout it — WE DID IT' — arms and open mouths fire together and you get the honest one. Leave headroom above both hands and keep their shoulder line level.
lighting: Flat frontal light from one large source directly behind camera; nothing directional, so the shadows don't break the symmetry.
coaching: Symmetry punishes a height gap — if he towers over her, widen his stance an inch to bring his shoulder line down to hers.

title: Back-to-back profile with low bouquet
subject: couple
direction: Stand them spine to spine and have each of them turn the face the same way as their front foot, so you get two clean profiles instead of two three-quarters. Tell her: 'let the bouquet hang low and away from the dress so the flowers read against the white'. Ask him for both hands deep in the pockets, thumbs out, and one roll of the shoulders back — 'chest up, chin level, look past the edge of the frame'.
lighting: Broad soft frontal source with a large white bounce behind them, background pushed about a stop over so both profiles cut cleanly against it.
coaching: One of them always leans back and rounds the spine — call 'weight onto your front foot, touch only at the shoulder blades'.

title: Stacked profile with bouquet at waist
subject: couple
direction: Set her first at forty-five degrees to camera, then slide him directly behind so his chest just touches her shoulder blade, hands in pockets, standing tall. Give them one fixed point off the lens: 'both of you find the top of that door frame and stay there'. Ask her to bring the bouquet to her front hip and let her far arm drop behind his so no stray elbow breaks the silhouette, and keep his chin just above her hairline rather than resting on it.
lighting: Blown-out white backdrop with a large source straight on plus a kicker from behind camera-right, otherwise his pale suit merges into the background.
coaching: If he hangs back you get a floating head over her shoulder — say 'step in until your jacket brushes her arm'.

title: Head on shoulder, ankles crossed
subject: couple
direction: Build him first: both hands in the pockets, weight onto the far leg, then cross the near ankle over and rest that toe on the floor. Bring her in shoulder to shoulder, arms folded loosely across the waist, bouquet hanging from the lower hand, and have her tip only the temple onto his shoulder. Then hold the frame and say 'don't smile yet — now think of something you're not allowed to laugh at' and shoot the three frames after that.
lighting: One large octabox high and slightly camera-left on a mid-grey seamless, so both faces stay open and the grey drops half a stop behind them.
coaching: She presses the whole head down and flattens her hair against his shoulder — ask for 'temple only, neck long' and re-check the gap between their heads.

title: Hooked arm with bouquet chest-high
subject: couple
direction: Angle him slightly off camera with one hand in his pocket and the near foot crossed over, then have her hook her hand around his bicep and pull in until their arms are flush with no daylight between. Tell her to lift the bouquet to the bottom of her ribs and rotate it toward you — 'flowers face me, wrist soft'. Lay her cheekbone on his shoulder without letting the chin drop, and cue him 'lean your head her way, eyes back to me'.
lighting: Even wash from a large source just behind camera against white, kept a touch under so the ivory dress holds highlight detail rather than clipping.
coaching: The bouquet drifts up and eats her neckline — keep it below the bust and off-centre so the V of the dress still reads.

title: Eyes down to the bouquet
subject: bride
direction: Turn her shoulders about thirty degrees off the lens and let her carry the bouquet in both hands, low at the hips and held slightly away from the dress. Ask her to lower only the eyes to the flowers: 'chin stays exactly where it is, just drop your lashes'. Cue a slow exhale and release at the end of it, when the mouth settles into a half-smile instead of a held one.
lighting: Backlit through a scrim behind her with a white v-flat feathered in from camera-left, so the shoulders glow while the bouquet keeps detail.
coaching: Dropping the whole head kills the jawline and shows the part in her hair — eyes only, neck stays long.

title: Hand to the strap, direct gaze
subject: bride
direction: Keep her hips near square to camera but drop the far shoulder an inch so it stops reading as a passport frame, then bring the far hand up to rest fingertips on the opposite strap. Tell her 'fingers light — like you're checking the strap, not gripping it', and turn the ring toward the lens. Keep the bouquet low and mostly out of frame, then say 'eyes to me, and think about him walking in' for the look.
lighting: Soft source high and just left of the lens with a reflector under the chin, so the lace bodice keeps texture and the eye sockets don't go hollow.
coaching: That raised hand creeps up under the chin and looks staged — hold it at collarbone height with the elbow off the ribs.

title: Over the shoulder through the veil
subject: bride
direction: Send her body away from camera at forty-five degrees, then rotate only the head back until you can see both eyes and the far cheek is about to disappear. Pull the veil forward over the near shoulder so it frames the face, and float her hand up near the jaw without contact — 'hand hovers, don't press the skin'. Cue 'look at me like you just spotted him' and shoot the moment the smile reaches the eyes, not before.
lighting: Large soft source close and slightly above camera-right so the tulle catches and glows, with the wall behind pushed a stop hot to stop the veil going grey.
coaching: Over-rotating the head shortens the far eye and pops the neck tendons — stop the turn as soon as you lose the far ear.

title: Back turned, look over shoulder
subject: bride
direction: Turn her fully away so the camera reads the back of the dress and the veil falls straight down the spine, then bring only the head back over the near shoulder. Ask her to push that shoulder down as she turns — 'shoulder away from your ear' — or the trapezius bunches under the strap. Keep the chin slightly down and toward the shoulder and hold it closed-lip: 'small smile, like you're keeping a secret'.
lighting: Window-soft light from camera-right raking across her back so the lace strap and veil texture separate, with the background left to blow out behind the shoulder line.
coaching: She swings the hips round with the head and the whole twist unwinds — plant the feet and let only the spine and neck rotate.

title: Genuine laugh with bouquet high
subject: bride
direction: Angle her body a third away from the lens and have her hug the bouquet up against the ribs in both hands so the shoulders stay loose. Do not ask for a laugh — frame it, then say 'tell me what he did the first time you met' and keep shooting straight through the answer. Fire in bursts of three: the keeper is usually the second frame, after the mouth opens and before the eyes squeeze shut.
lighting: Broad frontal soft light with a second head lifting the veil from behind, so the tulle separates instead of dissolving into the white background.
coaching: A held laugh dies in two seconds and the chin rides up — reset with a new question rather than telling her to laugh again.

title: Hand on hip, bouquet dropped low
subject: bride
direction: Weight onto the back foot, hips turned away from camera, then plant the near hand on the hip bone with the elbow pushed back behind the body line. Tell her 'let the bouquet hang all the way down from the other hand — heavy arm', so the flowers clear the face and the waist. Bring the chin forward and a shade down, and cue 'big smile on three' so you catch the top of it rather than the fade.
lighting: Large soft source straight on with the backdrop lit separately to clean white, so the deep lace neckline stays open with no shadow line down the bodice.
coaching: The hip hand lands flat with the fingers spread — ask for a loose fist or fingertips only, and keep that elbow out of the silhouette.

title: Lapel grip with low camera angle
subject: groom
direction: Drop the camera to sternum height and tilt up a few degrees so the shoulders widen and the jawline firms. Turn his body forty-five degrees away, back hand deep in the trouser pocket, and bring the front hand up to close on the lapel just under the bow tie — 'grab it like you're about to walk out the door'. Then say 'no smile, breathe out, eyes back to the lens' and take three frames on the exhale.
lighting: Harder key from camera-left, feathered so the far side of the tuxedo falls to near-black and the jacket reads as shape rather than a flat slab.
coaching: Men clamp the elbow to the ribs and the arm vanishes into the jacket — have him lift the gripping elbow an inch so light gets underneath it.

title: Cufflink adjust with gaze off-camera
subject: groom
direction: Give him a job instead of a pose: 'fasten your left cufflink, slowly, and keep going until I say stop'. Angle the body away from the lens and ask for both hands up at mid-chest so the forearms make a triangle rather than hanging at the belt. Then call 'hands stay there — look at the far corner of the room', because the off-camera eyeline is what stops this reading as a catalogue shot.
lighting: Single soft source from camera-left at head height, close enough that the grey wall falls off behind him and the shadow under the jaw shapes the beard.
coaching: The hands sink to belt height and it starts to look like fidgeting — keep the cuff at the bottom of the ribcage where the key still reaches it.

title: Hands in pockets open laugh
subject: groom
direction: Put both thumbs out and hands into the front trouser pockets so the elbows stay away from the ribs and the jacket keeps its shape. Turn his shoulders about twenty degrees off the lens, then send his chin the other way, past your shoulder, and say 'look at where I just came from and tell me the worst part of the speech you wrote'. Fire through the whole laugh, not the first frame of it — the real one lands two beats after the joke.
lighting: One big soft source high and camera-left with a white bounce at his right elbow, so the black lapel keeps texture instead of blocking up against the white wall.
coaching: Hands sink too deep and the shoulders round forward — ask for 'thumbs outside, only the fingers in' and have him roll his shoulders back once before the next frame.

title: Tie adjust with upward gaze
subject: groom
direction: Have him take the knot between thumb and first two fingers and lift it toward the collar as if he is genuinely finishing the job — a real pull, not a hover. Keep that forearm close to the chest so the elbow does not break the bottom of the frame, then say 'eyes up to the top corner of the window, chin follows halfway'. Ask him to hold the tension and breathe out, and shoot as the jaw releases so the mouth stays closed but not clenched.
lighting: Hard-ish window light from camera-left skimming across the face to keep the shadow edge on the far cheek — it carves the jaw and separates him from the pale wall.
coaching: Most men grab the whole knot in a fist, which reads as a strangle — reset with 'three fingers only, like you are straightening it in a mirror'.

title: Buttoning jacket at window
subject: groom
direction: Stand him a metre off the window with his body square to the glass, then bring both hands to the top button and let him actually fasten it — the gesture only reads if the fingers are working. Say 'chest toward me, face back to the light' so the torso stays broad while the head turns three quarters into the window. Keep his weight on the back foot and his gaze level, out past the frame, not down at his own hands.
lighting: Directional window light straight into the face from camera-left, no fill, letting the far side of the suit fall two stops down so the navy reads as shape rather than a flat block.
coaching: The chin drifts down to watch the button and you lose both eyes — call 'hands know what they are doing, eyes stay on the window' before you shoot.

title: Three-quarter turn hands down
subject: groom
direction: Drop the hands out of frame entirely and let the whole picture be jaw, collar and bow tie. Turn his shoulders to camera-left, then rotate the head back the other way until you can just see the far eyelashes clear of the nose — say 'turn your face slowly toward the door, and stop when I say stop'. Ask for the mouth closed and the tongue off the roof of the mouth; a half-second exhale before the shutter kills the tight-lipped look.
lighting: Broad soft light from camera-right filling the near side of the face with a gentle falloff behind the ear, so the black tux edge separates from the off-white wall without a rim.
coaching: Over-rotate the head and the far eye disappears behind the nose bridge — back it off five degrees and check the eyelash line before you commit.

title: Both hiding behind raised bouquet
subject: couple
direction: Bring them temple to temple with her camera-left, then have all four hands stack under the bouquet and lift it until the stems clear both mouths and the top flowers sit just under the eyes. Say 'push your heads together until they touch, then push the flowers up until I can only see eyes'. Once they are set, tell them 'now open your eyes as wide as you can, like you got caught' — the comedy of the instruction is what makes the frame, and it plays even with stiff couples.
lighting: Flat frontal soft light with a second source on the white wall, keeping the bouquet's pastels clean and putting matching catchlights in all four eyes.
coaching: One of them ends up half a head higher and the frame goes lopsided — fix it before the flowers come up by asking the taller one to bend at the knees, never at the neck.

title: Cheek to cheek over blooms
subject: couple
direction: This one is lower and warmer than the full hide: hold the bouquet at chin height so her smile stays visible and only his mouth goes behind the roses. Press cheekbone to cheekbone with him camera-left and slightly behind her, and say 'her cheek in front, his cheek behind, no daylight between them'. Ask her to smile with her teeth and him to smile only with the eyes — the contrast between the two reads as him amused by her, not as two people posing.
lighting: Big soft source dead front and slightly above, feathered down onto the flowers so the blush tones stay open and neither face carries a shadow from the other.
coaching: He leans in with his neck and ends up with a double chin — have him step his whole body in behind her shoulder instead, then push the forehead forward and the chin slightly down.

title: Head-back laugh with waist hold
subject: couple
direction: Set him half a step behind her camera-right, his far hand flat on the small of her waist and his near hand in his trouser pocket so the arm does not cut across her dress. She holds the bouquet low in both hands and turns her chest to camera while her face goes up and back. Say 'tip your head back toward his shoulder and laugh out loud — do not wait for something funny, just start'. He looks down at her, never at you, and you shoot the second wave of the laugh when her shoulders drop.
lighting: Wide soft frontal source with a touch of extra height, so the laugh does not throw shadow into her eye sockets and the white backdrop stays clean behind both heads.
coaching: A forced laugh dies in about two seconds and leaves a grimace — give them a second prompt ('now tell him he laughs like his father') and shoot the reaction to that instead.

title: Bride sharp groom soft behind
subject: couple
direction: Build it in layers: she stands front and square-ish to camera, he stacks directly behind her right shoulder about forty centimetres back so he falls out of focus. Focus on her near eye and hold it there no matter what he does. Tell her 'chin toward your left shoulder, eyes back to me, and think about something you are not going to tell me', then tell him 'look at the camera over her shoulder, mouth closed, do not smile'. The gap between her sharp gaze and his blurred one is the whole picture, so keep him from creeping forward.
lighting: Soft light high and slightly camera-left with a wide white bounce below, so her collarbone and lace hold detail while he drops half a stop into the background.
coaching: He drifts forward into the focal plane and the layered effect collapses — mark his toes on the floor and check the distance again before every second frame.

title: Nose into hair from behind
subject: couple
direction: Bring him in behind her camera-right shoulder and wrap both his arms low around her waist, hands meeting just under the bouquet so his fingers read as one soft shape and not a claw. Have him press his nose into her hair at the temple, eyes closed, cheek warm against her head. Say to her 'ignore him completely — look off past my shoulder and let the smile come up slowly, like you just remembered something good'. Keep her chin level and her far shoulder rolled back so her neck stays long.
lighting: Soft key from camera-left at about forty-five degrees with a subtle falloff to camera-right, so his dark suit gains a shadow edge and her shoulder line stays the brightest thing in frame.
coaching: His face buries too deep and you lose his eyes and cheekbone entirely — pull him back until you can see the whole line from his brow to his mouth against her hair.

title: Side by side gaze upward
subject: couple
direction: Stand them shoulder to shoulder with a hand's width of air between the arms — this frame lives on the gap, not on contact. His hands go in his pockets, hers hold the bouquet low against the front of the dress. Then say 'both of you find the top corner of the room behind me and look at it like something just landed there'. Give her a small smile and let him stay neutral; count them in so the two chins lift together rather than one after the other.
lighting: Bright high-key set with the background lit a stop over the subjects, so the upward gaze keeps clean catchlights and both silhouettes cut hard against pure white.
coaching: Chins go too high and you shoot up both noses — cap it with 'lift your eyes first, then only as much chin as the eyes need'.

title: Head on shoulder to camera
subject: couple
direction: This is the safe one every family asks for, so nail it fast: he stands camera-left with both hands in his pockets, she tucks in behind his upper arm and rests her temple against his shoulder with the bouquet held low in her far hand. Angle both sets of shoulders about fifteen degrees inward so the bodies form a shallow V, then bring both faces square back to the lens. Say 'lean your head onto him, but keep your eyes on my lens' and count them into the smile so you get both mouths at the same moment.
lighting: Even soft frontal light with a large source close enough to wrap around his beard and her jaw, keeping skin tones matched across two different complexions.
coaching: She tilts the head but leaves a gap at the shoulder so it looks like a hover, not a lean — tell her to actually put weight on him and let him take it.

title: Backlit forehead touch in profile
subject: couple
direction: Turn them into full profile facing each other so the light source sits directly behind the gap between their heads, then bring the foreheads together and hold. Her upper hand goes around the back of his neck with the fingers relaxed and the ring turned outward, and the bouquet stays low between their chests. Say 'foreheads touching, eyes closed, and smile at the fact that you are being made to do this'. Meter for their skin and let the background blow out — expose for the faces or you will get two silhouettes.
lighting: Full backlight through a window with a bounce card just off the lens axis, so the rim wraps the hairlines and the fill keeps the shadow side of both faces open.
coaching: Flare washes the whole frame and contrast dies — flag the top of the lens with your hand or a card until the shadow side of her cheek snaps back.

title: Forehead to forehead, bouquet low
subject: couple
direction: Stand them toe-to-toe, then say 'step in until your foreheads touch, and stop there' so they don't overshoot into a kiss. Have her hold the bouquet in both hands at belly-button height and drop her elbows so the arms don't box out her waist. Tell them 'eyes closed, chins level, small smile only' and let them breathe out twice before you fire.
lighting: Broad backlit white cyc with a large source over the camera, exposing for skin so the background blows to clean paper and the tux edge stays defined.
coaching: Foreheads pressed too hard flattens both noses and lifts her chin — cue 'barely touching, like you're about to fall asleep' and reset her chin down a centimetre.

title: Groom forward, bride soft behind
subject: couple
direction: Put him a full step closer to you than her, angled so his far shoulder rolls away and both hands go in his trouser pockets — say 'thumbs out, elbows loose, don't dig in'. Focus on his near eye and let her fall completely soft behind his shoulder; tell her 'stay put, chin toward him, just a small smile, you're the background here'. Ask him for the closed-lip version first: 'don't smile with teeth, just think about her'.
lighting: Big soft source high and camera-left, letting the white wall behind her go a stop hot so her blurred shape reads as light, not clutter.
coaching: Photographers focus on the tie or the boutonniere and lose his eye at this aperture — always pull focus to the near iris and re-confirm before the second frame.

title: Depth stack with open grin
subject: couple
direction: Same stacked setup as the quiet version, but this one lives on his laugh — hand in the pocket, weight on the back foot, and you say 'tell me what she did this morning that you're not supposed to repeat'. Take the frame on the second beat of the laugh when the teeth are showing but the eyes have caught up. Keep her behind his near shoulder and cue her 'lean an inch left so I can see all of your face, not half of it'.
lighting: Frontal soft light with a touch of fill under the chin so a light suit doesn't clip while his skin keeps modelling on the shadow side.
coaching: A wide grin held too long turns rigid and the eyes go dead — reset with 'shake it out, look at the floor, back to me' rather than asking for another smile.

title: Cheek to cheek facing camera
subject: couple
direction: Set her front and slightly left, him a half-step behind with his chest against her back shoulder, and say 'bring your cheek down onto her hair and leave it there'. Run his near arm around her waist so the hand lands flat on her far hip — 'fingers together, not gripping'. She takes the bouquet in both hands and drops it to hip level; then 'both of you, eyes to me, breathe out, now smile'.
lighting: Soft key just off the camera axis with a plain textured wall two metres back so the wall reads warm grey and neither face casts onto the other.
coaching: His head lands too high and he loses his jawline against her hair — ask him to bend at the knees, not the neck, so their eye lines sit within a hand's width.

title: Ring hand flat on his lapel
subject: couple
direction: Bouquet goes into her far hand and drops all the way down out of the way; the ring hand comes up flat onto his lapel with fingers slightly spread — say 'soft hand, like you're checking his heartbeat, don't make a claw'. Rotate her wrist until the stone catches your key light and the back of the hand faces you square. He keeps one hand in his pocket, and you cue them both: 'look at me and tell me you're stuck with each other now'.
lighting: Large soft source camera-left, high enough to put a specular kick on the stone while keeping the white gown from clipping.
coaching: Tense fingers and a bent wrist make the hand look twice its size — reset with 'shake the hand out, place it, relax the knuckles' and shoot immediately.

title: Ring hand raised by her cheek
subject: couple
direction: This is the ring shot with the hand held high, not on him — bring her palm up beside her own cheek at eye height and say 'fingers open and relaxed, elbow tucked in to your ribs'. His arm goes around her back so the hand appears on her far waist and he carries the bouquet on his side, keeping her raised arm unobstructed. Cue the reaction, not the pose: 'react like you've just been told the ring is real'.
lighting: Even frontal soft light on a white sweep so both white outfits separate on tone alone; add a hair light if his shoulder merges with the background.
coaching: A raised elbow that swings out from the body reads as a wave and covers her jaw — keep the elbow pinned to the ribs and the palm just clear of the cheekbone.

title: Head tipped back onto his cheek
subject: couple
direction: He stands directly behind her and slightly off her right shoulder; she tips her head back and to the side until her temple finds his cheek — 'let the weight of your head go, he's holding it'. His hands come around her waist and disappear behind the bouquet, which she carries high in both hands so the greenery breaks the line of her hips. Both eyes closed: 'chins down a touch, no smile, just breathe'.
lighting: Directional soft light from camera-right at head height so her collarbones and his jaw both catch it, with the background held clean and bright behind them.
coaching: She usually tips her head backward instead of sideways and shows the underside of her chin — correct with 'ear toward your own shoulder, not the ceiling'.

title: Temple kiss from her left
subject: couple
direction: Bring him in from her left in near-profile and stop his mouth at her hairline — 'lips just above her ear, and hold it, don't peck'. She stays open to camera with the bouquet high in both hands, eyes closed and the smile kept small: cue her 'eyes shut, and think about what he whispered'. Shoot two or three frames through the hold; the first one always has tension in her mouth.
lighting: Hard backlight blown out behind them with a scrim feathered onto her face, so his dark suit reads as a solid silhouette shape on the left third.
coaching: His nose disappears into her hair and the kiss stops reading — pull him back until you can see a sliver of background between his profile and her cheek.

title: Face in her hair, eyes down
subject: couple
direction: Crop tight to her face and let him enter frame as a half-face on the right, forehead and nose buried in her hair just behind the ear — 'press in and stay, you're not in this photo, you're the frame'. She looks down toward the bouquet with her eyes almost closed: say 'lids heavy, look at the flowers, not the floor'. Wait for the moment her mouth softens on its own; the held smile is always the wrong frame here.
lighting: Single large soft source camera-left at her eye level, wrapping across her cheek so his side of the frame falls a stop and a half down into shadow.
coaching: At this crop a dropped chin kills the eye and leaves only lashes — keep the chin level and move only the eyes downward.

title: Arm wrapped across from behind
subject: couple
direction: She stands front with the veil falling on her far side; he steps in behind and reaches his arm all the way across her ribs so the hand rests at her far waist — 'wrap her, don't hover'. His other hand comes up loosely near his own lapel to fill the gap under his chin. Bouquet drops low in her outside hand, both faces angle back to camera: 'heads together, small smiles, don't grin'.
lighting: Flat, even frontal light on white for a clean catalogue look; add a rim from behind camera-right if his black jacket loses its edge.
coaching: The crossing arm cuts straight across her bust line if it sits too high — slide it down to the natural waist so it follows the narrowest part of her.

title: Hands over his eyes from behind
subject: couple
direction: Hand him the bouquet in both hands at his waist, then bring her up behind his shoulder and say 'cover his eyes and don't tell him what's coming'. Her palms go flat over his eyes with fingers together and the ring hand on top; her face pops out beside his ear, not behind it. Trigger the laugh with a line at him: 'guess where she's taking you tonight' — shoot the whole exchange, the best frame is his answer, not the setup.
lighting: Bright even key close to the camera axis with plenty of fill, so the flat white background and the moving hands both stay clean at a shutter you can freeze on.
coaching: She usually stands too far behind and only half her face makes the frame — cue 'chin over his shoulder, cheek almost touching his' before you say anything funny.
